topics.title: Introduction to Monitoring and Evaluation
topics.description: An introduction to the fundamental concepts, purposes and processes of Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) in healthcare programmes.
keyPoints: Monitoring is a continuous process involving the systematic collection and analysis of data to track programme progress against established objectives.
Evaluation is a systematic process of assessing the relevance, effectiveness, efficiency and impact of programme activities to determine whether objectives have been achieved.
Monitoring and Evaluation involves collecting, analysing and using data to track performance and inform decision-making.
M&E helps programmes assess progress, identify implementation gaps and improve service delivery.
The results chain provides a framework for understanding how programme resources and activities contribute to intended results.
M&E findings support evidence-informed planning, programme improvement and accountability.
subtopics: Basic concepts and definitions of Monitoring and Evaluation
Reasons for undertaking Monitoring and Evaluation
Using M&E information for programme decision-making

topics.title: Data Collection and Reporting Tools
topics.description: Understanding routine healthcare data collection and reporting tools, their purposes, formats, frequencies and relationships.
keyPoints: Routine M&E tools are used to collect, document, report and analyse information about services provided by healthcare workers.
Harmonised and standardised tools promote consistency in healthcare data collection and reporting.
Data collection and reporting tools may be maintained in paper or electronic formats.
Cards generally contain information about one individual and are commonly used to document information from an encounter.
Forms collect information about an individual and may contain multiple sheets or sections. They are commonly completed during service delivery.
Registers contain individual client records arranged in rows, with standard data elements recorded in columns.
Monthly summary forms aggregate service information and do not contain individual client-level records.
Information recorded in forms and registers contributes to monthly reporting and programme monitoring.
subtopics: Cards: purpose, content and frequency of use
Forms: purpose, content and frequency of use
Registers: individual records, rows and columns
Monthly summary forms: aggregation and reporting
Paper-based and electronic data collection formats
Relationship between forms, registers and monthly summary forms
Harmonised and standardised healthcare reporting tools

topics.title: HIV Testing Services (HTS) Monitoring and Evaluation Tools
topics.description: An introduction to the harmonised HIV Testing Services monitoring and evaluation tools and their role in documenting and monitoring HTS activities.
keyPoints: HTS monitoring tools support the documentation, reporting and monitoring of HIV testing services.
Healthcare workers should understand the purpose and appropriate use of each harmonised HTS tool.
HTS 001 is the HIV Testing Services Form.
HTS 002 is the HIV Testing Services Register.
HTS 003 is the Index Contact Testing Form.
HTS 004 is the HIV Testing Services Monthly Summary Form.
The tools support the recording of client-level information, service delivery activities and aggregated programme data.
The presentation outlines an HTS service flow that includes pre-test counselling and risk assessment, HIV testing, syphilis testing, post-test counselling and result disclosure.
Eligible HIV-negative clients may be referred for PrEP services.
subtopics: Purpose of HTS monitoring and evaluation
Referral of eligible HIV-negative clients for PrEP

topics.title: HTS Tools: Sections, Components and Completion
topics.description: Practical understanding of the sections and components of HTS monitoring tools and how healthcare workers complete the required documentation.
keyPoints: Healthcare workers should be familiar with the sections and components of the harmonised HTS tools.
HTS forms are used to document relevant client-level information during service delivery.
The HTS register supports the systematic recording of individual client records.
The Index Contact Testing Form supports documentation of index contact testing activities.
The HTS Monthly Summary Form is used to aggregate and report relevant service information.
Information should be recorded accurately and consistently in the appropriate tool.
The information documented in service delivery tools supports programme monitoring and reporting.
Client information should be handled confidentially and stored securely.
subtopics: Identifying the sections and components of HTS tools
Completing HTS 003: Index Contact Testing Form
Completing HTS 004: HTS Monthly Summary Form
Accuracy and completeness of HTS records
Confidentiality and secure storage of HTS documentation

topics.title: PrEP and PEP Monitoring Tools
topics.description: Understanding the revised Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) and Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) monitoring tools and their use in HIV prevention programme documentation and reporting.
keyPoints: PrEP and PEP monitoring tools support documentation and monitoring of HIV prevention services.
The PrEP and PEP Screening and Eligibility Form captures client-level information on HIV and STI risk assessment and eligibility.
The screening and eligibility form is completed at every client encounter by the relevant service provider.
The screening form includes demographic information, pre-test counselling and risk assessment, HIV testing and PrEP eligibility sections.
The PrEP and PEP Card tracks services provided to clients enrolled in PrEP or PEP and is updated at each clinical encounter.
The PrEP and PEP Register documents client information and programme interventions and supports cohort analysis and monthly reporting.
The register includes facility details, registration and personal information, PrEP initiation and follow-up, PEP documentation, discontinuation and ART linkage.
Accurate client-level and aggregate data recording supports programme monitoring.
subtopics: Introduction to PrEP and PEP monitoring
PrEP and PEP Screening and Eligibility Form
PrEP and PEP Card: front, centre and back pages
Storage and confidentiality of PrEP and PEP records

topics.title: STI Monitoring and Reporting Tools
topics.description: Understanding the monitoring and reporting of sexually transmitted infection services using the relevant programme documentation and reporting tools.
keyPoints: STI monitoring and reporting tools support documentation of STI-related service delivery and programme performance.
Accurate recording helps healthcare workers monitor services and report programme activities.
STI screening and syndromic assessment are important elements of service documentation.
Relevant information may include client screening, clinical assessment, diagnosis, treatment and referral.
STI service information contributes to programme monitoring and monthly reporting.
Reported information may be disaggregated by relevant characteristics such as age, sex and target population, as specified by the reporting tool.
Completeness and consistency of STI records are important for reliable programme data.
subtopics: Introduction to STI monitoring and reporting
Completeness and accuracy of STI records

topics.title: Viral Hepatitis Patient Monitoring Tools
topics.description: Understanding patient-level monitoring and documentation tools used in viral hepatitis services, including hepatitis B and hepatitis C care.
keyPoints: Viral hepatitis patient monitoring tools support the documentation and tracking of services provided to clients.
The tools support monitoring of hepatitis B and hepatitis C services.
Patient monitoring documentation supports the recording of relevant service and clinical information over time.
Hepatitis C treatment and retreatment information should be documented where applicable.
Follow-up testing, including Sustained Virological Response (SVR) assessment, is part of the monitoring information covered in the training.
Patient monitoring may include treatment outcomes and relevant follow-up information.
Documentation supports continuity of care, programme monitoring and reporting.
Accurate and complete patient records are essential for reliable service monitoring.
subtopics: Hepatitis B and hepatitis C patient monitoring
Hepatitis C treatment and retreatment documentation
Follow-up and Sustained Virological Response (SVR) testing

topics.title: Data Quality, Error Correction and Confidentiality
topics.description: Understanding common data quality problems, appropriate error correction, record review and the importance of protecting confidential healthcare information.
keyPoints: Data quality is essential for reliable programme monitoring, reporting and decision-making.
Common documentation problems include missing, incomplete, illegible, duplicated and inconsistent entries.
Physical and logical errors can affect the accuracy and reliability of healthcare records.
Healthcare workers should identify and address errors using the appropriate documentation procedures.
Regular review of registers and reporting tools helps identify data quality gaps.
Supportive supervision can strengthen documentation practices and improve data quality.
Healthcare records should be stored securely and accessed only by authorised personnel.
Client confidentiality must be maintained throughout data collection, storage, analysis and reporting.
subtopics: Identification and correction of documentation errors
Prevention of recurring data quality problems
Register review and routine data checks
Supportive supervision and data quality improvement
Confidentiality and appropriate access to client information

topics.title: Viral Hepatitis Monthly Summary and Reporting
topics.description: Understanding the aggregation and reporting of viral hepatitis service information using monthly summary and relevant programme reporting tools.
keyPoints: Monthly reporting summarises and aggregates relevant information about services provided.
Viral hepatitis reporting draws on relevant patient monitoring and service documentation tools.
Information from facility and community service delivery may contribute to programme reporting where applicable.
Relevant laboratory and treatment records support the documentation and reporting process.
Accurate aggregation is important to ensure that reported figures reflect the underlying service records.
Facility-level information contributes to the broader programme reporting structure.
Reporting supports programme monitoring, performance assessment and decision-making.
Confidentiality should be maintained when handling and reporting client information.
subtopics: Introduction to viral hepatitis monthly reporting
Facility, LGA, State and National reporting structure
Data accuracy and completeness during reporting

topics.title: Practical Exercises and Group Work
topics.description: Applying the knowledge gained from the training through practical exercises, case scenarios, tool completion and group-based data management activities.
keyPoints: Practical exercises help participants apply M&E concepts to routine healthcare documentation.
Participants practise identifying the appropriate tools for different service delivery scenarios.
HTS case scenarios help participants identify the relevant tools required for client documentation.
PrEP, PEP, STI and viral hepatitis exercises reinforce understanding of their respective monitoring tools.
Participants practise identifying data sources and transferring relevant information into the appropriate tools.
Data quality exercises help participants identify missing, inconsistent and incorrect entries.
Group work encourages discussion, shared learning and practical problem-solving.
The exercises reinforce accurate documentation, reporting and confidentiality.
subtopics: Practical exercises on Monitoring and Evaluation
HTS case scenarios and tool identification
Identifying data sources and reporting requirements
Data quality checks and error correction
